description: Construction of a single storey building to facilitate the creation of 1 x studio residential dwelling (Use Class C3). Associated works to include hard and soft landscaping, boundary treatment, refuse and recycling storage facilities and bicycle parking provision. All works in connection with the subdivision of land at 173 Grove Road.
decision_conditions:
The principle of residential development
is acceptable within the location. However, due to the incongruous design of
the building by reason of its diminutive form it is viewed as an anomaly within
the streetscene, incompatible with the existing built form and an ineffective
use of the land contrary to Policy 19 and 53 of the adopted Waltham Forest
Local Plan Part 1 (2024).

The proposed development provides
a poor standard of accommodation for future occupiers in relation to (i) an internal
storage area that fails to comply with minimum space standards, (ii) the
bedroom space located in an incompatible area creating a dead frontage resulting
in the loss of natural surveillance (iii) an external amenity space that fails
to comply with minimum space standards. Therefore, the proposal would be
contrary to Policy 56 (Residential Space Standards) of the Waltham Forest Local
Plan LP1 (2024), Policy D6 of The London Plan (2021), London Plan Guidance –
Housing Design Standards (June 2023) and the Urban Design SPG (2010)

In the absence of a satisfactory
Outline Construction Logistic Plan, a full assessment of how the proposed
development would be built or serviced without severely affecting the public
highway could not be made in line with Policies T7 of the London Plan (2021)
and Policy 65 of the Waltham Forest Local Plan LP1 (2024).

The applicant failed to enter
into a s106 agreement and therefore not in compliance with Policy 94
(Infrastructure and Developer Contributions) of the Waltham Forest Local Plan
LP1 (2024) (figures applicable at the time of the assessment of the
application):Car Free Development - the
development is to be classified as car-free and residents will not be eligible
for parking permits.A condition survey of the
adjoining carriageway/footwayS106 Financial contribution of £650.00
towards the Epping Forest SAMMA S106 Financial contribution of
£250 is requested toward CLP monitoring.A S106 contribution of £1,000 is
requested toward improving walking and cycling facilities within the sites
vicinity which will directly benefit future residents of the site.S278 agreement to remove the
existing vehicle crossover on Salisbury Road in front of the site; renewal of
the footway and kerb along the frontage of the site and Extension of the
existing on-street parking bays across the site frontage.











Financial contribution of 5% for
s106 monitoring fees.
